prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a low-speed head-on collision in Pearland, Texas, and has back strain. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1138; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for agreeing to give this recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather not give my full name on a recording, but you can use the claim number.

Q: That's fine. Can you describe where you were when the collision happened?
A: I was driving south on the main road in Pearland, heading to the grocery store. It was a clear afternoon, and traffic was moderate.

Q: Walk me through what happened right before impact.
A: The other car came over into my lane. I braked and swerved a little, but we still hit nose to nose. It wasn't a hard hit, more of a jolt.

Q: What was your speed at the time?
A: Maybe twenty-five or thirty miles an hour. I was already slowing for the light up ahead.

Q: Did either airbag deploy?
A: No, they didn't. My seatbelt was on, and I didn't hit my head on anything.

Q: Did you get out of the vehicle at the scene?
A: Yes, but I felt stiff. My lower back started aching within an hour or so.

Q: Have you sought medical treatment since the accident?
A: I went to urgent care the next day. They said I had a back strain and gave me a muscle relaxer and told me to rest and do some stretching.

Q: Are you still experiencing symptoms?
A: Some days are better than others. Sitting for long periods bothers me, and I've had to skip a few shifts at work.

Q: Have you had any prior injuries to your back?
A: Nothing serious. I had a minor strain years ago, but it healed fine and I didn't need a doctor for it.

Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add to your statement?
A: Only that I'm trying to get back to normal and I appreciate you checking in on how I'm doing.

Q: Thank you. This concludes the statement.
